messages:
ana: quick follow-up on the ops split idea for fallback probing — thinking we should decouple quality probing from the runtime decision path. runtime should only surface lightweight signals (latency, token-loss, entropy) and the profile service should own the heavy quality checks. thoughts?

mike: +1. the runtime touching full-quality probes will blow up p50/p95 unless we shard it off.

sophia: agree. runtime signal should be tiny. propose: runtime emits a probe_id header when it samples a request, and a sidecar/collector picks up full request+response for offline shadow eval.

tony: sampling rate vs cost is the tricky bit. if we sample too much we pay a lot for evals (and possible customer data handling). do we have an initial rate proposal?

ana: (typo) ana: ha — initial thought 0.1% global, higher for canaries. also require scrubbers before storing. privacy is mandatory.

mike: scrubbers + ephemeral storage. we should avoid routing raw user text to third-party evalers; run shadow-eval in our private cluster by default. for dedicated/private customers we can offer a customer-owned eval endpoint.

sophia: operational flow sketch:
- runtime: when sample triggered, attach probe_id and minimal metrics (latency_ms, token_entropy, token_loss_est) to request metadata.
- collector: pulls full request/response from local cache using probe_id, strips PII, uploads to shadow-eval queue.
- shadow-eval service: runs golden comparison, computes degradation_score and regression buckets, pushes result back to profile-service.
- profile-service: correlates with recent rollouts and can trigger automated rollback or escalate to ops.

ana: pseudoconfig for probe consumer:```json
{"quant_probe_enabled": true, "sample_rate": 0.001, "scrub_mode": "scrub-pii", "eval_target": "shadow-eval-prod", "rollback_threshold": 0.12}
```

tony: that looks good. rollout_threshold semantics? 0.12 = 12% of sampled queries exceed some degscore?

sophia: yeah degscore definition: weighted combination of semantic drift (embedding distance), completion-accuracy (task-specific metrics), and hallucination heuristics. we need to nail that metric in the RFC.

mike: runtime API change note: add optional probe_id in request metadata and an enum `probe_reason` (canary|random|scheduled). default off. backwards compatible.

ana: question: for precision fallbacks, should the runtime attempt immediate cheaper fallbacks (fp8->int8->int4) based on perf only, or consult profile-service first?

sophia: do perf-first for p95-sensitive endpoints. but before promoting a new quant profile we must shadow-eval it for at least X hours. runtime fallbacks (inference-time) should be perf-driven with a safety guard: if recent probe_degradation_rate > threshold, prefer a conservative fallthrough.

tony: operationally: fallback precedence should be configurable per endpoint. default: {fp8,int8,int4,fp16}. add flag `quality_guard_window` to allow history-driven override.

mike: need disk/globally consistent store for probe results — time-series plus last-known-good profile per model+endpoint. profile-service should expose the current allowed cascade list via the runtime config API.

sophia: also add a lightweight heartbeat metric: `probe_ack_rate` so ops can see if probes are being processed. alert if ack_rate < 80% for 10m.

ana: quick security note: for private deployments we need to support a customer-owned shadow-eval endpoint and encryption-at-rest for probe artifacts. add that to the security checklist.

deploy-bot: probe-gate v0.1 deployed to staging (ana/mike/sophia canary) :rocket:

mike: can someone turn that pseudoconfig into an ops-runbook snippet? i'll sketch the runtime changes in an RFC PR.

sophia: i'll draft the degradation_score spec and a minimal test harness (will include embedding-distance and rule-based hallucination detectors).

tony: ok - sounds like we have an approach. next actionable: ana open RFC for ops split + runtime api change; sophia draft degscore; mike draft runbook. :thumbsup:
